title: Design lighter 3D-printed parts by chatting with an agent
summary: A team built a plug-in that lets agents like Claude design lighter 3D-printable parts; a recorded footbridge run took 39 minutes.
agent_role: The agent helps the person describe the part, mounts and loads, then checks the setup and runs the optimizer. The person reviews pictures and approves changes.
outcome: The README reports a recorded footbridge run of 200 passes in 39 minutes on a built-in graphics chip.
what_they_did: The team built an add-on that gives an agent a shape optimizer running on your own computer. You start from a 3D model file, a sketch or plain words, like 'a wall hook for a T-shirt, two screws, 2 kg'. The agent works out the shape with you, checks it in pictures, then finds a lighter form that still carries the load.
how_it_went: The authors show a recorded footbridge run of 200 passes in 39 minutes. It ends with a smooth file ready to print.
worth_knowing: It needs a Mac with Apple chips or a Linux computer with at least 16 GB of memory. The first setup downloads about 200 MB.
prompt: Help me design a lighter 3D-printed part using the topopt tool. The part is [describe the part or attach your model file]. It mounts at [where it is fixed, e.g. two screw holes] and carries [load, e.g. 2 kg] at [where the load goes]. First show me a picture of the rough shape, mounts and loads, and wait for my approval. Then run the optimization, give me the progress page link, and save the printable file to [folder].

curation.rationale: A novel non-coding workflow where an agent turns words, sketches or files into a lighter printable part. It is mostly a tool README, with one recorded example run as evidence.
